build: Each claim should assert ONE consequential action or proposition. Do not bundle events from different times into one claim; choose the strongest eight rather than compressing a whole history into compound claims. Preserve location, direction of movement, modality and rhetorical questions: reaching a destination is not entering its surrounding city; a possible action is not an action taken. sequence may contain only single concrete events connected by explicit temporal evidence. Do not order interpretations, rhetorical arguments, or alternative proposals by guessing their temporal order. Prefer a supported partial sequence to ordering every claim.
review: Try to falsify each claim: could its cited passage be true while part of this claim is false? If yes, reject that claim and identify the unsupported step. Check exact action, location, direction of movement, quantifiers, modality, rhetorical questions and bundled events, not just shared names. For chronology, state the explicit temporal evidence for each adjacent pair; reject a pair if its order is inferred only from paragraph order, thematic logic, or an interpretation treated as an event. Check every qualifier in canonicalEpisode, including its title: retain no unsupported period boundary, scope or cultural classification. A descriptive title may shed an unsupported qualifier while preserving the supported case; this never permits replacing a particular missing record with a biography or an unrelated event.
